overview:
usage: dataforge <command> [--flag value ...]

Commands, by phase:
  load:
    load              Read a CSV file into a new frame Handle and report its shape.
  profile:
    describe-columns  Read full column profiles off a profile Handle, flagged columns first.
    describe-target   Read one declared target's problem type and statistics off a profile Handle.
    missingness       Read how missing values spread across rows, and which columns go missing together.
    profile           Profile a frame once into a profile Handle and return its Dataset Digest.
    top-associations  List the most strongly associated column pairs off a profile Handle, strongest first.
    value-summary     Read one column's top values, rare labels, bounds and percentiles off a profile Handle.
  workspace:
    export-frame      Write a frame Handle's data as a CSV file in the Workspace and return its path.
    list-handles      List the Workspace's Handles newest first, each with its Lineage and size.

Go deeper:
  dataforge <command> --help    one command: flags, result, errors, an example
  dataforge schema <command> <argument> [path]
                                one nested argument's schema, one level at a time
  The `dataforge` Skill (SKILL.md) teaches the workflow and what each exit code asks.

Every command prints one JSON value on stdout, errors too. Exit codes: 0 success,
2 InvalidInput, 3 UnknownName, 4 Conflict, 5 Infeasible, 6 IncompatibleArtifact,
1 Unexpected. A list of records prints as {"fields": [...], "rows": [[...], ...]}.

Workspace Settings, set by the Operator; leave them as they are:
  --workspace, --literal-policy, --declared-inputs, --core-budget
--progress prints one line per Pipeline Event to stderr.

commands.describe-columns:
usage: dataforge describe-columns --profile <string> [--names <array>] [--flagged-only <boolean>] [--offset <integer>] [--limit <integer>]

Read full column profiles off a profile Handle, flagged columns first.

Use when:
  Call this after `profile` to read more about columns than the Dataset Digest shows:
  every statistic for the column's semantic type, the missing-value counts, the flags
  and how the type was decided. It reads the stored profile only, so it is cheap and
  never recomputes. It holds no cell values; for top values, bounds and percentiles call
  `value_summary`. Filter with `names` or `flagged_only`, then page with `offset` and
  `limit`. The same arguments always return the same page.

Flags (a flag left out is null, which means its default):
  --profile <string>, required
      A profile Handle, such as `profile_7f3a9c2e`.
  --names <list of string>, optional
      Only these columns. Null means every profiled and skipped column.
  --flagged-only <true|false>, optional
      True keeps only columns that raised a flag. Null means false.
  --offset <integer>, optional
      How many matching columns to skip, for the next page. Null means 0. Constraints:
      at least 0.
  --limit <integer>, optional
      Most columns to return, from 1 to 15. Null means 15. Constraints: at least 1; at
      most 15.

Returns DescribeColumnsResult, as one JSON object:
  profile: string
      The profile Handle read.
  total: integer
      How many columns match the filters.
  offset: integer
      How many matching columns this page skipped.
  columns: table of (column, role, semantic_type, numeric_kind, dtype, parsed_dtype, type_flags, flags, cardinality, missingness, stats)
      Matching columns: flagged ones first, then dataset order. At most 15; when more
      remain, `omitted` counts them and names `describe_columns`.
  flag_dials: table of (flag, dials)
      One entry per flag raised on a column of this page, in `columns` order of first
      appearance.
  Every result also has `warnings` (caveats; read them first) and `omitted` (cut lists,
  each naming the command that returns the rest).

Errors (Error Code, exit code):
  unknown_handle (3)
      `profile` names no profile Handle in this Workspace. `candidates` lists profile
      Handles, newest first.
  wrong_handle_kind (2)
      `profile` is a Handle of another kind.
  unknown_column (3)
      A name in `names` is not a column of the profile. `candidates` lists close
      matches; `issues` lists every unknown name.
  invalid_argument (2)
      An argument has the wrong type or is out of its range.
  incompatible_artifact (6)
      Another library format version wrote `profile`.
  invalid_setting (2)
      A Workspace Setting is invalid. The message names it and its source.

See Also:
  missingness: Read every co-missing pair.
  profile: Make the profile Handle and its Dataset Digest.
  value-summary: Read one column's top values, bounds and percentiles.

Cost: reads only stored records; it does not grow with the data.

Example:
  $ dataforge load --path train.csv
  {...,"frame":"frame_7f3a9c2e",...}
  $ dataforge profile --frame frame_7f3a9c2e
  {...,"profile":"profile_1b2c3d4e",...}
  $ dataforge describe-columns --profile profile_1b2c3d4e --names age,city
  {"warnings":...,"omitted":...,"profile":"profile_1b2c3d4e","total":2,"offset":0,...}
commands.describe-target:
usage: dataforge describe-target --profile <string> --name <string>

Read one declared target's problem type and statistics off a profile Handle.

Use when:
  Call this after `profile` with `targets` set, to see what kind of learning problem a
  target poses and what to watch for: missing target values, class imbalance or a skewed
  numeric target. A classification target lists its most common classes with their
  labels; a regression target gives its distribution. Class labels are cell values, so
  they are Literal Fields. To rank features against the target, call `top_associations`
  with `column` set to it. It reads the stored profile only, so it is cheap and never
  recomputes.

Flags (a flag left out is null, which means its default):
  --profile <string>, required
      A profile Handle, such as `profile_7f3a9c2e`.
  --name <string>, required
      A target declared when the profile was made.

Returns DescribeTargetResult, as one JSON object:
  profile: string
      The profile Handle read.
  column: string
      The target column.
  problem_type: one of regression|binary_classification|multiclass_classification|unknown
      The learning problem the target implies.
  missing_count: integer
      Rows whose target is missing.
  missing_ratio: number
      Share of rows whose target is missing.
  flags: list of one of contains_missing|high_imbalance|severe_imbalance|highly_skewed|is_identifier
      Problems with the target: `contains_missing`, `high_imbalance` (dominant class
      ratio above 5), `severe_imbalance` (above 20), `highly_skewed` or `is_identifier`.
  distribution: object
      Statistics of a numeric target, as `describe_columns` gives them; null for a
      classification target.
  classes: object
      Classes of a classification target; null for a regression target.
  Every result also has `warnings` (caveats; read them first) and `omitted` (cut lists,
  each naming the command that returns the rest).

Errors (Error Code, exit code):
  unknown_handle (3)
      `profile` names no profile Handle in this Workspace. `candidates` lists profile
      Handles, newest first.
  wrong_handle_kind (2)
      `profile` is a Handle of another kind.
  unknown_column (3)
      `name` is not a target declared on the profile. `candidates` lists the declared
      targets closest to it.
  invalid_argument (2)
      An argument has the wrong type.
  incompatible_artifact (6)
      Another library format version wrote `profile`.
  invalid_setting (2)
      A Workspace Setting is invalid. The message names it and its source.

See Also:
  profile: Declare targets and make the profile Handle.
  top-associations: Rank features against the target.
  value-summary: Read every class label, or a target's bounds and percentiles.

Cost: reads only stored records; it does not grow with the data.

Example:
  $ dataforge load --path train.csv
  {...,"frame":"frame_7f3a9c2e",...}
  $ dataforge profile --frame frame_7f3a9c2e --targets income
  {...,"profile":"profile_1b2c3d4e",...}
  $ dataforge describe-target --profile profile_1b2c3d4e --name income
  {...,"column":"income","problem_type":"regression","missing_count":1,...}
commands.export-frame:
usage: dataforge export-frame --frame <string>

Write a frame Handle's data as a CSV file in the Workspace and return its path.

Use when:
  Call this to hand a frame on as a file: a split fold, an imputed frame, or a loaded
  one. The file goes into the Workspace's `exports/` folder, named after the Handle; you
  cannot choose where it goes. Exporting the same Handle again returns the same path and
  writes nothing, because a frame never changes. A CSV keeps no dtypes, so reading it
  back may infer types again. Exporting never changes the Handle: to change the data,
  change the declarations and call the Operation that made it again.

Flags (a flag left out is null, which means its default):
  --frame <string>, required
      A frame Handle, such as `frame_7f3a9c2e`.

Returns ExportFrameResult, as one JSON object:
  path: string
      Absolute path of the CSV, inside the Workspace's `exports/` folder.
  Every result also has `warnings` (caveats; read them first) and `omitted` (cut lists,
  each naming the command that returns the rest).

Errors (Error Code, exit code):
  unknown_handle (3)
      `frame` names no frame Handle in this Workspace. `candidates` lists up to 5 frame
      Handles, newest first.
  wrong_handle_kind (2)
      `frame` is a Handle of another kind. `allowed` names `frame`.
  incompatible_artifact (6)
      Another library format version wrote `frame`. Load it again.
  invalid_argument (2)
      `frame` is missing or not a string.
  invalid_setting (2)
      A Workspace Setting is invalid. The message names it and its source.

See Also:
  list-handles: Find a frame Handle to export.
  load: Make a frame Handle from a CSV file.

Cost: grows with the data. On large data, run it in the background or with a longer
timeout.

Example:
  $ dataforge load --path train.csv
  {...,"frame":"frame_7f3a9c2e",...}
  $ dataforge export-frame --frame frame_7f3a9c2e
  {"warnings":...,"omitted":...,"path":".../exports/frame_7f3a9c2e.csv"}
commands.list-handles:
usage: dataforge list-handles [--kind <kind>] [--offset <integer>] [--limit <integer>]

List the Workspace's Handles newest first, each with its Lineage and size.

Use when:
  Call this to find Handles made earlier: after a restart, as a sub-agent sharing the
  Workspace, or when you have lost track of a Handle string. Each Handle comes with its
  Lineage, which is the Operation that made it, the arguments it was passed, and the
  Handles it read. Read the Lineage to tell two Handles of the same kind apart. Handles
  never expire and are never deleted, so an old Handle stays usable. This reads only
  stored records, never dataset rows.

Flags (a flag left out is null, which means its default):
  --kind <one of frame|profile|routing|recipe|unit|imputer|c2st>, optional
      Only Handles of this kind: `frame`, `profile`, `routing`, `recipe`, `unit`,
      `imputer` or `c2st`. Null lists every kind.
  --offset <integer>, optional
      How many of the newest Handles to skip, for the next page. Null means 0.
      Constraints: at least 0.
  --limit <integer>, optional
      Most Handles to return, from 1 to 12. Null means 12. Constraints: at least 1; at
      most 12.

Returns ListHandlesResult, as one JSON object:
  total: integer
      How many Handles of the asked kind exist in the Workspace.
  offset: integer
      How many of the newest Handles this page skipped.
  handles: table of (handle, kind, operation, arguments, inputs, size)
      Handles, newest first. At most 12; when more remain, `omitted` counts them and
      names `list_handles`.
  Every result also has `warnings` (caveats; read them first) and `omitted` (cut lists,
  each naming the command that returns the rest).

Errors (Error Code, exit code):
  invalid_argument (2)
      `kind` is not a Handle kind, or `offset` or `limit` is out of range.
  invalid_setting (2)
      A Workspace Setting is invalid. The message names it and its source.

See Also:
  export-frame: Write a frame Handle out as CSV.
  load: Make a frame Handle from a CSV file.

Cost: reads only stored records; it does not grow with the data.

Example:
  $ dataforge load --path train.csv
  {...,"frame":"frame_7f3a9c2e",...}
  $ dataforge list-handles --kind frame
  {"warnings":...,"omitted":...,"total":1,"offset":0,
  "handles":{"fields":["handle","kind","operation","arguments","inputs","size"],
  "rows":[["frame_7f3a9c2e","frame","load",
  {"fields":["name","value","value_cut"],"rows":[["path","\"train.csv\"",false]]},
  [],{"fields":["measure","value"],"rows":[["rows",6],["columns",3]]}]]}}
commands.load:
usage: dataforge load --path <string>

Read a CSV file into a new frame Handle and report its shape.

Use when:
  Call this first, once per dataset. If the Operator declared inputs, only those paths
  load, and any other path is refused, including an edited copy of a declared file. With
  none declared, any CSV path loads. Every later Operation reads the data through the
  returned frame Handle: a short string such as `frame_7f3a9c2e` naming the stored
  frame, which never changes. Loading the same path twice makes two Handles over
  identical data.

Flags (a flag left out is null, which means its default):
  --path <string>, required
      Path of the CSV file, exactly as you were given it. A relative path is resolved
      from the working directory.

Returns LoadResult, as one JSON object:
  frame: string
      Frame Handle for the loaded data, such as `frame_7f3a9c2e`.
  n_rows: integer
      Number of data rows, not counting the header.
  n_columns: integer
      Number of columns, including any not listed in `columns`.
  columns: table of (column, dtype)
      Columns in CSV header order, at most 100. Past 100, `omitted` counts the rest.
  Every result also has `warnings` (caveats; read them first) and `omitted` (cut lists,
  each naming the command that returns the rest).

Errors (Error Code, exit code):
  input_not_declared (2)
      The Operator declared inputs and `path` is not one of them. Nothing is loaded or
      written.
  input_not_found (2)
      No file exists at `path`.
  invalid_argument (2)
      `path` is missing or not a string.
  invalid_setting (2)
      A Workspace Setting is invalid. The message names it and its source.
  unexpected (1)
      The file could not be read as CSV. Stop and report it.

See Also:
  export-frame: Write a frame Handle out as CSV.
  list-handles: Find frame Handles made earlier in this Workspace.

Cost: grows with the data. On large data, run it in the background or with a longer
timeout.

Example:
  $ dataforge load --path train.csv
  {"warnings":{"fields":["code","message","columns","param","hint"],"rows":[]},
  "omitted":{"fields":["field","shown","total","operation"],"rows":[]},
  "frame":"frame_7f3a9c2e","n_rows":6,"n_columns":3,
  "columns":{"fields":["column","dtype"],
  "rows":[["age","Int64"],["city","String"],["income","Float64"]]}}
commands.missingness:
usage: dataforge missingness --profile <string> [--column <string>] [--offset <integer>] [--limit <integer>]

Read how missing values spread across rows, and which columns go missing together.

Use when:
  Call this after `profile` when columns have missing values, to decide whether to drop
  rows and whether values are missing at random. It gives how many values each row is
  missing, and the column pairs whose missing values fall on the same rows, most co-
  missing first. Columns that go missing together suggest the values are missing for a
  reason, which matters for imputation. It reads the stored profile only, so it is cheap
  and never recomputes. The same arguments always return the same page.

Flags (a flag left out is null, which means its default):
  --profile <string>, required
      A profile Handle, such as `profile_7f3a9c2e`.
  --column <string>, optional
      Only pairs that include this column, which is then always `column_a`. Null means
      every pair.
  --offset <integer>, optional
      How many matching pairs to skip, for the next page. Null means 0. Constraints: at
      least 0.
  --limit <integer>, optional
      Most pairs to return, from 1 to 100. Null means 100. Constraints: at least 1; at
      most 100.

Returns MissingnessResult, as one JSON object:
  profile: string
      The profile Handle read.
  sparsity: number
      Share of all cells that are missing.
  columns_with_missing: integer
      Profiled columns missing at least one value.
  rows: object
      How many values each row is missing.
  total: integer
      How many pairs match the filter. Only columns missing at least one value form
      pairs.
  offset: integer
      How many matching pairs this page skipped.
  pairs: table of (column_a, column_b, correlation, mar_suspect)
      Matching pairs, most co-missing (highest `correlation`) first, ties in dataset
      order. At most 100; when more remain, `omitted` counts them and names
      `missingness`.
  mar_suspect_dial: object
      The `profile` dial behind `mar_suspect`.
  Every result also has `warnings` (caveats; read them first) and `omitted` (cut lists,
  each naming the command that returns the rest).

Errors (Error Code, exit code):
  unknown_handle (3)
      `profile` names no profile Handle in this Workspace. `candidates` lists profile
      Handles, newest first.
  wrong_handle_kind (2)
      `profile` is a Handle of another kind.
  unknown_column (3)
      `column` is not a column of the profile. `candidates` lists close matches.
  invalid_argument (2)
      An argument has the wrong type or is out of its range.
  incompatible_artifact (6)
      Another library format version wrote `profile`.
  invalid_setting (2)
      A Workspace Setting is invalid. The message names it and its source.

See Also:
  describe-columns: Read each column's missing-value counts.
  profile: Make the profile Handle and its Dataset Digest.

Cost: reads only stored records; it does not grow with the data.

Example:
  $ dataforge load --path train.csv
  {...,"frame":"frame_7f3a9c2e",...}
  $ dataforge profile --frame frame_7f3a9c2e
  {...,"profile":"profile_1b2c3d4e",...}
  $ dataforge missingness --profile profile_1b2c3d4e
  {"warnings":...,"omitted":...,"profile":"profile_1b2c3d4e",...,"columns_with_missing":2,...}
commands.profile:
usage: dataforge profile --frame <string> [--semantic-types <json>] [--numeric-kinds <json>] [--sentinels <json>] [--datetime-formats <json>] [--targets <array>] [--exclude-columns <array>] [--skip-columns <array>] [--seed <integer>] [--thresholds <json>]

Profile a frame once into a profile Handle and return its Dataset Digest.

Use when:
  Call this once per frame, right after `load`. It computes every column statistic,
  association and nonlinearity probe once and stores them in a profile Handle, which
  carries its frame. Every later step reads the profile, never the raw data. The Dataset
  Digest is the dataset at low resolution: row and column counts, duplicates, sparsity,
  targets, your declarations, and one row per column with flagged columns first. It
  holds no cell values. Declarations made here, and those the frame inherited, are
  recorded on the profile and passed down to every frame made from it. To change a
  declaration or a dial, call `profile` again; that makes a new profile Handle and
  leaves the old one as it was.

Flags (a flag left out is null, which means its default):
  --frame <string>, required
      A frame Handle, such as `frame_7f3a9c2e`.
  --semantic-types <JSON, inline or @file.json>, optional
      Semantic types you set instead of detection, one entry per column.
      Fields: dataforge schema profile semantic_types
  --numeric-kinds <JSON, inline or @file.json>, optional
      Numeric kinds you set instead of detection, one entry per numeric column.
      Fields: dataforge schema profile numeric_kinds
  --sentinels <JSON, inline or @file.json>, optional
      Values that mean "missing" in a column, one entry per column.
      Fields: dataforge schema profile sentinels
  --datetime-formats <JSON, inline or @file.json>, optional
      How to read datetime columns, one entry per column.
      Fields: dataforge schema profile datetime_formats
  --targets <list of string>, optional
      Target columns. Null means none.
  --exclude-columns <list of string>, optional
      Columns to leave out of this and every later phase, added to what the frame
      already excludes. Null means none.
  --skip-columns <list of string>, optional
      Columns profiling skips but later phases still see. Null means none.
  --seed <integer>, optional
      Seed for every random step: mixture fits, mutual information and the nonlinearity
      probes. Null means a fixed default, so the same call gives the same result.
      Constraints: at least 0; at most 4294967295.
  --thresholds <JSON, inline or @file.json>, optional
      Dials, grouped by what they judge, each with its default and range.
      Fields: dataforge schema profile thresholds

Returns ProfileResult, as one JSON object:
  profile: string
      Profile Handle, such as `profile_7f3a9c2e`. It carries its frame and these
      declarations.
  frame: string
      The frame Handle that was profiled.
  n_rows: integer
      Number of rows.
  n_columns: integer
      Number of columns in the frame, excluded ones included.
  duplicate_rows: integer
      Number of rows that repeat an earlier row exactly.
  duplicate_ratio: number
      Share of rows that repeat an earlier row.
  sparsity: number
      Share of all cells that are missing.
  targets: table of (column, problem_type, missing_ratio)
      Declared targets and their problem types.
  declarations: object
      Your declarations as recorded on the profile.
  columns: table of (column, role, semantic_type, numeric_kind, null_ratio, severity, cardinality, skew, outlier_density, flags)
      Profiled and skipped columns: flagged ones first, then dataset order. At most 100;
      past 100, `omitted` counts the rest and names `describe_columns`.
  flag_dials: table of (flag, dials)
      One entry per flag raised on any column, in `columns` order of first appearance.
  Every result also has `warnings` (caveats; read them first) and `omitted` (cut lists,
  each naming the command that returns the rest).

Errors (Error Code, exit code):
  unknown_handle (3)
      `frame` names no frame Handle in this Workspace. `candidates` lists frame Handles,
      newest first.
  wrong_handle_kind (2)
      `frame` is a Handle of another kind.
  unknown_column (3)
      A declaration names a column the frame lacks. `candidates` lists close matches;
      `issues` lists every problem argument.
  duplicate_key (2)
      A declaration list names the same column twice.
  declaration_conflict (4)
      Two declarations contradict: a numeric kind on a column declared non-numeric, a
      target that is excluded or skipped, or a declaration that differs from one the
      frame inherited.
  invalid_dial_value (2)
      Two dials are out of order, such as `severity_minor` above `severity_moderate`.
  invalid_argument (2)
      An argument has the wrong type or is out of its range.
  override_coercion_failed (5)
      No value of a column converts to its declared type.
  incompatible_artifact (6)
      Another library format version wrote `frame`.
  invalid_setting (2)
      A Workspace Setting is invalid. The message names it and its source.

See Also:
  list-handles: Find profile Handles made earlier.
  load: Make the frame Handle to profile.

Cost: grows with the data. On large data, run it in the background or with a longer
timeout.

Example:
  $ dataforge load --path train.csv
  {...,"frame":"frame_7f3a9c2e",...}
  $ dataforge profile --frame frame_7f3a9c2e --targets income
  {...,"profile":"profile_1b2c3d4e","frame":"frame_7f3a9c2e","n_rows":6,"n_columns":3,...}
commands.top-associations:
usage: dataforge top-associations --profile <string> [--column <string>] [--metric <metric>] [--min-strength <number>] [--offset <integer>] [--limit <integer>]

List the most strongly associated column pairs off a profile Handle, strongest first.

Use when:
  Call this after `profile` to find columns that go together: near-duplicates to drop,
  predictors for imputation, or the features most related to a target. Pearson (two
  numeric columns), Cramér's V (two categorical columns) and η² (a numeric and a
  categorical column) come in one list sorted by strength, the absolute value of the
  measure. Set `column` to a target to rank features against it. Pairs whose measure
  could not be computed are left out. It reads the stored profile only, so it is cheap
  and never recomputes. The same arguments always return the same page.

Flags (a flag left out is null, which means its default):
  --profile <string>, required
      A profile Handle, such as `profile_7f3a9c2e`.
  --column <string>, optional
      Only pairs that include this column, which is then always `column_a`. Null means
      every pair.
  --metric <one of pearson|cramers_v|eta_squared>, optional
      Only this metric: `pearson`, `cramers_v` or `eta_squared`. Null means all three.
  --min-strength <number>, optional
      Only pairs at least this strong, from 0 to 1. Null means no floor. Constraints: at
      least 0; at most 1.
  --offset <integer>, optional
      How many matching pairs to skip, for the next page. Null means 0. Constraints: at
      least 0.
  --limit <integer>, optional
      Most pairs to return, from 1 to 100. Null means 100. Constraints: at least 1; at
      most 100.

Returns TopAssociationsResult, as one JSON object:
  profile: string
      The profile Handle read.
  total: integer
      How many pairs match the filters.
  offset: integer
      How many matching pairs this page skipped.
  pairs: table of (column_a, column_b, metric, value, near_redundant)
      Matching pairs by strength, strongest first; ties by metric (`pearson`,
      `cramers_v`, `eta_squared`), then dataset order. At most 100; when more remain,
      `omitted` counts them and names `top_associations`.
  near_redundant_dials: table of (metric, dial)
      For each metric, the dial behind `near_redundant`.
  Every result also has `warnings` (caveats; read them first) and `omitted` (cut lists,
  each naming the command that returns the rest).

Errors (Error Code, exit code):
  unknown_handle (3)
      `profile` names no profile Handle in this Workspace. `candidates` lists profile
      Handles, newest first.
  wrong_handle_kind (2)
      `profile` is a Handle of another kind.
  unknown_column (3)
      `column` is not a column of the profile. `candidates` lists close matches.
  invalid_argument (2)
      An argument has the wrong type or is out of its range.
  incompatible_artifact (6)
      Another library format version wrote `profile`.
  invalid_setting (2)
      A Workspace Setting is invalid. The message names it and its source.

See Also:
  describe-target: Read a target's problem type and statistics.
  missingness: Read which columns go missing together.
  profile: Make the profile Handle and its Dataset Digest.

Cost: reads only stored records; it does not grow with the data.

Example:
  $ dataforge load --path train.csv
  {...,"frame":"frame_7f3a9c2e",...}
  $ dataforge profile --frame frame_7f3a9c2e --targets income
  {...,"profile":"profile_1b2c3d4e",...}
  $ dataforge top-associations --profile profile_1b2c3d4e --column income
  {...,"profile":"profile_1b2c3d4e","total":1,"offset":0,"pairs":{"fields":["column_a","column_b","metric","value","near_redundant"],"rows":[["income","city","eta_squared",...,true]]},...}
commands.value-summary:
usage: dataforge value-summary --profile <string> --column <string> [--k <integer>]

Read one column's top values, rare labels, bounds and percentiles off a profile Handle.

Use when:
  Call this to see a column's actual values: to spot sentinels such as `-999` or `"?"`
  that stand for missing values, to learn the labels a categorical column uses, or to
  check a column's range. These are cell values, so each one is in a Literal Field;
  every other detail Operation holds none. To read a spotted sentinel as missing, call
  `profile` again with it in `sentinels`. It reads the stored profile only, so it is
  cheap and never recomputes.

Flags (a flag left out is null, which means its default):
  --profile <string>, required
      A profile Handle, such as `profile_7f3a9c2e`.
  --column <string>, required
      A column of the profile.
  --k <integer>, optional
      Most entries in each list, from 1 to 20. Null means 20. Constraints: at least 1;
      at most 20.

Returns ValueSummaryResult, as one JSON object:
  profile: string
      The profile Handle read.
  column: string
      The column summarised.
  semantic_type: one of numeric|categorical|datetime|boolean|text|identifier
      The column's semantic type; null when it was skipped.
  cardinality: integer
      Number of distinct non-missing values; null when skipped.
  top_values: table of (value, count, share)
      The most common values, most common first. The profile keeps up to 10 for a
      categorical, boolean or whole-number column and none for a continuous one;
      `omitted` counts the rest.
  rare_labels: list of true|false or integer or number or string or null
      Labels of a categorical column rarer than
      `thresholds.categorical.stratification_rare_threshold_pct` of `profile`, most
      common first. A Literal Field.
  bounds: object
      The smallest and largest value of a numeric or datetime column; else null.
  median: true|false or integer or number or string or null
      The median of a numeric column; else null. A Literal Field.
  mode: true|false or integer or number or string or null
      The most common value; null for a datetime or text column. A Literal Field.
  percentiles: table of (percentile, value)
      Percentiles of a numeric column, lowest first; empty for any other type.
  Every result also has `warnings` (caveats; read them first) and `omitted` (cut lists,
  each naming the command that returns the rest).

Errors (Error Code, exit code):
  unknown_handle (3)
      `profile` names no profile Handle in this Workspace. `candidates` lists profile
      Handles, newest first.
  wrong_handle_kind (2)
      `profile` is a Handle of another kind.
  unknown_column (3)
      `column` is not a column of the profile. `candidates` lists close matches.
  invalid_argument (2)
      An argument has the wrong type or is out of its range.
  incompatible_artifact (6)
      Another library format version wrote `profile`.
  invalid_setting (2)
      A Workspace Setting is invalid. The message names it and its source.

See Also:
  describe-columns: Read a column's statistics without cell values.
  profile: Declare sentinels and make the profile Handle.

Cost: reads only stored records; it does not grow with the data.

Example:
  $ dataforge load --path train.csv
  {...,"frame":"frame_7f3a9c2e",...}
  $ dataforge profile --frame frame_7f3a9c2e
  {...,"profile":"profile_1b2c3d4e",...}
  $ dataforge value-summary --profile profile_1b2c3d4e --column city --k 2
  {...,"column":"city","semantic_type":"categorical","cardinality":3,"top_values":{"fields":["value","count","share"],"rows":[["north",2,...],["south",2,...]]},...}

describe-columns.profile:
profile: string, required
  A profile Handle, such as `profile_7f3a9c2e`.
describe-columns.names:
names: list of string, optional
  Only these columns. Null means every profiled and skipped column.
describe-columns.flagged_only:
flagged_only: true|false, optional
  True keeps only columns that raised a flag. Null means false.
describe-columns.offset:
offset: integer, optional
  How many matching columns to skip, for the next page. Null means 0. Constraints: at
  least 0.
describe-columns.limit:
limit: integer, optional
  Most columns to return, from 1 to 15. Null means 15. Constraints: at least 1; at most
  15.

describe-target.profile:
profile: string, required
  A profile Handle, such as `profile_7f3a9c2e`.
describe-target.name:
name: string, required
  A target declared when the profile was made.

export-frame.frame:
frame: string, required
  A frame Handle, such as `frame_7f3a9c2e`.

list-handles.kind:
kind: one of frame|profile|routing|recipe|unit|imputer|c2st, optional
  Only Handles of this kind: `frame`, `profile`, `routing`, `recipe`, `unit`, `imputer`
  or `c2st`. Null lists every kind.
list-handles.offset:
offset: integer, optional
  How many of the newest Handles to skip, for the next page. Null means 0. Constraints:
  at least 0.
list-handles.limit:
limit: integer, optional
  Most Handles to return, from 1 to 12. Null means 12. Constraints: at least 1; at most
  12.

load.path:
path: string, required
  Path of the CSV file, exactly as you were given it. A relative path is resolved from
  the working directory.

missingness.profile:
profile: string, required
  A profile Handle, such as `profile_7f3a9c2e`.
missingness.column:
column: string, optional
  Only pairs that include this column, which is then always `column_a`. Null means every
  pair.
missingness.offset:
offset: integer, optional
  How many matching pairs to skip, for the next page. Null means 0. Constraints: at
  least 0.
missingness.limit:
limit: integer, optional
  Most pairs to return, from 1 to 100. Null means 100. Constraints: at least 1; at most
  100.

profile.frame:
frame: string, required
  A frame Handle, such as `frame_7f3a9c2e`.
profile.semantic_types:
semantic_types: list of object, optional
  Semantic types you set instead of detection, one entry per column. Null means detect
  every column.

Fields:
  column: string
      Column name, exactly as in the data.
  semantic_type: one of numeric|categorical|datetime|boolean|text|identifier
      The semantic type: `numeric`, `categorical`, `datetime`, `boolean`, `text` or
      `identifier`.
profile.numeric_kinds:
numeric_kinds: list of object, optional
  Numeric kinds you set instead of detection, one entry per numeric column. Null means
  detect them.

Fields:
  column: string
      Column name, exactly as in the data. Its semantic type must be `numeric`.
  numeric_kind: one of continuous|bounded_discrete
      `continuous`, or `bounded_discrete` for a whole-number count or score with a small
      range.
profile.sentinels:
sentinels: list of object, optional
  Values that mean "missing" in a column, one entry per column. Null means none beyond
  blank strings and the default text markers.

Fields:
  column: string
      Column name, exactly as in the data.
  values: list of number or list of string
      The values to read as missing: all numbers for a numeric column, or all strings
      for a text column. For a text column they replace the default markers (`NA`,
      `NULL`, `?`...) and match case-insensitively. Constraints: at least 1 items; at
      least 1 items.
profile.datetime_formats:
datetime_formats: list of object, optional
  How to read datetime columns, one entry per column. Null means infer each format.

Fields:
  column: string
      Column name, exactly as in the data.
  format: string, optional
      A strftime format for a text column, such as `%Y-%m-%d` or `%Y` for bare years; or
      null.
  epoch_unit: one of s|ms|us|ns|d, optional
      The unit of a numeric epoch column: `s`, `ms`, `us`, `ns` or `d`; or null.
profile.targets:
targets: list of string, optional
  Target columns. Null means none.
profile.exclude_columns:
exclude_columns: list of string, optional
  Columns to leave out of this and every later phase, added to what the frame already
  excludes. Null means none.
profile.skip_columns:
skip_columns: list of string, optional
  Columns profiling skips but later phases still see. Null means none.
profile.seed:
seed: integer, optional
  Seed for every random step: mixture fits, mutual information and the nonlinearity
  probes. Null means a fixed default, so the same call gives the same result.
  Constraints: at least 0; at most 4294967295.
profile.thresholds:
thresholds: object, optional
  Dials, grouped by what they judge, each with its default and range. Null keeps every
  default.

Fields:
  missingness: object, optional
      Missing-value severity and the missingness flags.
      Fields: dataforge schema profile thresholds missingness
  type_detection: object, optional
      How each column's semantic type is detected.
      Fields: dataforge schema profile thresholds type_detection
  numeric: object, optional
      Skew, kurtosis, tails, outliers and the numeric flags.
      Fields: dataforge schema profile thresholds numeric
  categorical: object, optional
      Rare labels and the categorical flags.
      Fields: dataforge schema profile thresholds categorical
  correlation: object, optional
      Near-redundancy and mutual information between columns.
      Fields: dataforge schema profile thresholds correlation
  datetime: object, optional
      The datetime flags.
      Fields: dataforge schema profile thresholds datetime
  nonlinearity: object, optional
      The nonlinearity probes routing reads.
      Fields: dataforge schema profile thresholds nonlinearity
profile.thresholds.missingness:
thresholds.missingness: object, optional
  Missing-value severity and the missingness flags.

Fields:
  severity_minor: number, optional
      Null ratio below which a column's severity is `minor`. Must not exceed
      `severity_moderate`. Null means 0.01. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  severity_moderate: number, optional
      Null ratio below which severity is `moderate`. Must not exceed `severity_high`.
      Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  severity_high: number, optional
      Null ratio below which severity is `high`; at or above it, `severe`. Null means
      0.2. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  mar_correlation_threshold: number, optional
      Correlation between two columns' missing masks above which both are flagged
      `missingness.mar_suspect`. Null means 0.6. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  col_drop_threshold: number, optional
      Null ratio above which a column is flagged `missingness.drop_candidate`. Null
      means 0.5. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  row_drop_threshold: number, optional
      Share of profiled columns a row must be missing to count as a drop-candidate row.
      Null means 0.5. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
profile.thresholds.type_detection:
thresholds.type_detection: object, optional
  How each column's semantic type is detected.

Fields:
  numeric_coerce_threshold: number, optional
      Share of a text column's values that must parse as numbers for it to be read as
      numeric. Null means 0.95. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  datetime_coerce_threshold: number, optional
      Share of a text column's values that must parse as datetimes for it to be read as
      datetime. Null means 0.8. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  encoded_category_max_unique: integer, optional
      Most distinct values an integer column may have to be read as an encoded category.
      Null means 15. Constraints: at least 1.
  encoded_category_max_ratio: number, optional
      Most distinct values per non-null row an integer column may have to be read as an
      encoded category. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  identifier_unique_ratio: number, optional
      Distinct values per row above which a column is read as an identifier. Null means
      0.99. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  identifier_max_median_length: integer, optional
      Longest median length, in characters, a text column may have to be read as an
      identifier. Null means 40. Constraints: at least 1.
  free_text_avg_words: integer, optional
      Median word count above which a text column is read as free text. Null means 3.
      Constraints: at least 1.
  free_text_median_chars: integer, optional
      Median length, in characters, above which a multi-word text column is read as free
      text. Null means 20. Constraints: at least 1.
  free_text_p90_chars: integer, optional
      90th-percentile length, in characters, above which a high-cardinality text column
      is read as free text. Null means 35. Constraints: at least 1.
  free_text_min_unique_ratio: number, optional
      Distinct values per row a text column needs, with `free_text_p90_chars`, to be
      read as free text. Null means 0.4. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  free_text_high_unique_with_spaces: number, optional
      Distinct values per row above which a multi-word text column is read as free text
      whatever its length. Null means 0.7. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
profile.thresholds.numeric:
thresholds.numeric: object, optional
  Skew, kurtosis, tails, outliers and the numeric flags.

Fields:
  skew_normal: number, optional
      Largest absolute skew still graded `normal`. Must not exceed `skew_moderate`. Null
      means 0.5. Constraints: at least 0.
  skew_moderate: number, optional
      Largest absolute skew graded `moderate`. Must not exceed `skew_high`. Null means
      1.0. Constraints: at least 0.
  skew_high: number, optional
      Largest absolute skew graded `high`; above it, `severe`. Null means 2.0.
      Constraints: at least 0.
  kurt_platykurtic_upper: number, optional
      Excess kurtosis below which a column is platykurtic. Must be below
      `kurt_leptokurtic_lower`. Null means -1.0.
  kurt_leptokurtic_lower: number, optional
      Excess kurtosis above which a column is leptokurtic. Null means 3.0.
  near_constant_threshold: number, optional
      Share of rows holding the most common value above which a column is flagged
      `numeric.near_constant`. Null means 0.9. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  scale_orders_of_magnitude: integer, optional
      Orders of magnitude a column's values must span to be flagged
      `numeric.scale_anomaly`. Null means 3. Constraints: at least 1.
  bimodal_dip_p_value_threshold: number, optional
      Dip-test p-value below which a column is tested further for `numeric.bimodal`.
      Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  bimodal_min_separation_threshold: number, optional
      Least separation (Ashman's D) between two modes for `numeric.bimodal`. Null means
      2.0. Constraints: at least 0.
  bimodal_min_component_weight: number, optional
      Least share of rows in the smaller mode for `numeric.bimodal`. Null means 0.05.
      Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  tail_asymmetry_right_share_threshold: number, optional
      Right-tail share above which a column's tails are `right_heavy`. Must exceed
      `tail_asymmetry_left_share_threshold`. Null means 0.6666666666666666. Constraints:
      at least 0; at most 1.
  tail_asymmetry_left_share_threshold: number, optional
      Right-tail share below which a column's tails are `left_heavy`. Null means
      0.3333333333333333. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  outlier_sigma_threshold: number, optional
      Standard deviations from the mean beyond which a value counts as an outlier. Null
      means 3.0. Constraints: at least 0.
  high_outlier_density_threshold: number, optional
      Share of outlier values above which a column is flagged
      `numeric.high_outlier_density`. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0; at most
      1.
profile.thresholds.categorical:
thresholds.categorical: object, optional
  Rare labels and the categorical flags.

Fields:
  rare_threshold_pct: number, optional
      Share of rows below which a category counts as rare. Null means 0.01. Constraints:
      at least 0; at most 1.
  stratification_rare_threshold_pct: number, optional
      Share of rows below which a category counts as a rare label the stratified split
      protects. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  mixed_type_min_minor_pct: number, optional
      Least share (lower confidence bound) of the minority value type, numbers or text,
      for `categorical.mixed_type`. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  near_constant_threshold: number, optional
      Share of rows holding the most common value above which a column is flagged
      `categorical.near_constant`. Null means 0.9. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
profile.thresholds.correlation:
thresholds.correlation: object, optional
  Near-redundancy and mutual information between columns.

Fields:
  near_redundant_pearson_threshold: number, optional
      Absolute Pearson or Spearman correlation above which two numeric columns are near-
      redundant. Null means 0.95. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  near_redundant_cramer_v_threshold: number, optional
      Cramér's V above which two categorical columns are near-redundant. Null means 0.8.
      Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  near_redundant_eta_squared_threshold: number, optional
      η² above which a numeric and a categorical column are near-redundant. Null means
      0.5. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  mi_min_rows: integer, optional
      Fewest rows with both a feature and the target present to estimate their mutual
      information. Null means 10. Constraints: at least 1.
profile.thresholds.datetime:
thresholds.datetime: object, optional
  The datetime flags.

Fields:
  mnar_null_ratio_threshold: number, optional
      Null ratio, unparseable values included, above which a column is flagged
      `datetime.mnar_suspected`. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  high_gap_cv_threshold: number, optional
      Coefficient of variation of the gaps between dates above which a column is flagged
      `datetime.high_gap_variance`. Null means 1.0. Constraints: at least 0.
  recent_window_fraction: number, optional
      Latest share of the date range checked for `datetime.recent_date_missing`. Null
      means 0.1. Constraints: at most 1; greater than 0.
profile.thresholds.nonlinearity:
thresholds.nonlinearity: object, optional
  The nonlinearity probes routing reads.

Fields:
  spearman_pearson_discrepancy_threshold: number, optional
      Largest Spearman-minus-Pearson gap over predictors above which a column reads as
      monotonic nonlinear. Null means 0.1. Constraints: at least 0; at most 2.
  mutual_information_threshold: number, optional
      Mean excess mutual information, in nats, above which a column reads as complex
      nonlinear. Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0.
  r2_gap_threshold: number, optional
      Random-forest R² minus linear R² above which a column reads as complex nonlinear.
      Null means 0.1. Constraints: at least 0.
  heteroscedasticity_p_value_threshold: number, optional
      Breusch-Pagan p-value below which a column's residuals count as heteroscedastic.
      Null means 0.05. Constraints: at least 0; at most 1.
  r2_rf_unpredictable_threshold: number, optional
      Random-forest R² below which a column reads as unpredictable. Null means 0.05.
      Constraints: at most 1.
  min_rows: integer, optional
      Fewest complete rows, across a column and its predictors, to probe it. Null means
      20. Constraints: at least 2.
  bootstrap_sample_size: integer, optional
      Most rows sampled for the R² probes. Null means 500. Constraints: at least 2.
